The Velvet Door — Guitar Card

The aria, unplugged. Key of D minor, unhurried — about 76 BPM. Verses and pre-choruses: arpeggio over the full chords. Choruses: power chords, strummed. One chord per line; the chord sits above the word where it changes. Sing it where it lives in your chest.

Hear the melody first

Not strumming — a lead line built on the hook, played over Verse 1, the Pre-Chorus and the Chorus, with the chord roots underneath so you can hear the changes coming. Play it, hum it, steal it.

Download the MIDI Download the MP3

The shapes

POWER CHORDS — one shape, slid everywhere.
Index on the root, ring finger two frets up on the next string.
Strum only the strings under your fingers.

D5            Bb5           F5
e|--x--       e|--x--       e|--x--
B|--x--       B|--x--       B|--x--
G|--7--       G|--3--       G|--x--
D|--7--       D|--3--       D|--3--
A|--5--       A|--1--       A|--3--
E|--x--       E|--x--       E|--1--

C5            A5
e|--x--       e|--x--
B|--x--       B|--x--
G|--5--       G|--2--
D|--5--       D|--2--
A|--3--       A|--0--
E|--x--       E|--x--

FULL CHORDS — for the arpeggio parts (numbers run fat E string to high e)
Dm — x x 0 2 3 1        (open, easy)
Bb — x 1 3 3 3 x        (index A-string fret 1; ring flattens the
                          middle three at fret 3; mute the high e)
F  — x x 3 2 1 1        (the cheat F — or Fmaj7: x x 3 2 1 0)
C  — x 3 2 0 1 0        (open, easy)
A  — x 0 2 2 2 0        (open, easy)

Pattern & strum

THE ONE ARPEGGIO PATTERN (every full chord, six plucks)
1. Thumb — the root (lowest string of the shape)
2. Index — 3rd string (G)
3. Middle — 2nd string (B)
4. Ring — 1st string (high e)
5. Middle — 2nd string again
6. Index — 3rd string again
Up the stairs and back down. One pattern per line; twice if a line
feels empty.

STRUMMING THE CHORUSES: two slow down-strums per line to start, let
them ring. When the rust shakes off: Down, Down, Down-Up per line.

The hook

THE HOOK — nine notes: D – F – A – D – C – A – F – E – D
All inside the Dm grip, first position. Play it as the intro,
between sections, and once at the very end.

e|---------------------1--0--------
B|-----3--1-----------------3-----
G|--------2-----2-----------------
D|--0--3--------------------------
A|--------------------------------
E|--------------------------------

Or hold the Dm shape and arpeggiate the same nine notes in order —
only the C moves (2nd string, 1st fret) and the E is the open top string.

The song — chords over lyrics

VERSE 1 — arpeggio, full chords
Dm
You leave your masks beside the door,
Bb
The hall keeps every word we said.
F
A silver thread across the floor,
A
A rose gone dark beside the bed.

PRE-CHORUS — arpeggio, a little more deliberate
Dm
I hear the house draw in its breath,
C
The old clock hesitates to chime.
Bb
You ask me what I fear the most—
A
I fear the choice was always mine.

CHORUS — POWER CHORDS, strummed, let it open up
F5
Come through the curtain, call me by my name,
C5
Where every vow is beautiful and strange.
D5
I'll meet you where the velvet meets the stone;
A5
I won't be claimed, and I won't leave alone.
(the A5 hangs — the next verse's Dm answers it)

VERSE 2 — arpeggio
Dm
Your letter bears a bloodystain,
Bb
The ink runs red beneath my thumb.
F
Outside, the rain taps out refrain;
A
Inside, the locked room answers none.

PRE-CHORUS — arpeggio
Dm
You say the past can be undone,
C
You say the key is in your hand.
Bb
But every door we open here
A
Leads somewhere neither understands.

CHORUS — power chords
F5
Come through the curtain, call me by my name,
C5
Where every vow is beautiful and strange.
D5
I'll meet you where the velvet meets the stone;
A5
I won't be claimed, and I won't leave alone.

BRIDGE — arpeggio, slowest yet, let every note die
Dm
If love is only taking, let the silence answer.
Bb
If fear can wear a golden face, I know it now.
Dm
I'll keep the key, I'll choose the morning,
A
And leave the final word unspoken.  (hang on the A)

FINAL CHORUS — power chords; the last line comes home
F5
Come through the curtain, call me by my name,
C5
No borrowed promise gets to bind me to its flame.
D5
I'll meet you where the velvet meets the stone;
Dm   (full chord, one slow arpeggio)
I choose the door, I choose my way back home.

OUTRO — arpeggio, barely there
Dm
The gloves are gone; the clock strikes four.
Dm
I leave the key outside the door.
(then play the hook once, and let the last Dm ring)

If Dm sits high in your natural voice when you try it, tell Ira — the whole card drops a few steps, same shapes, same hook, friendlier throat. This card is just for the porch: not part of the programme.
